interactionPlan.concept: A vertical corner acts as an accidental aperture, projecting light from a hidden scene onto the ground so that hidden motion can be reconstructed over time.
learningObjectives: Understand how a vertical edge acts as a 1D pinhole-style aperture by blocking light rays at specific angles
Explain how subtle, sub-visual changes in diffuse ground reflection can be processed to track hidden moving objects
Interpret a spatio-temporal (angle vs. time) plot to determine the path and count of hidden moving targets
interactionPlan.keyInsight: A simple wall corner acts as an accidental lens-less camera, translating the angular positions of hidden moving objects into distinct, trackable patterns of light and shadow on the ground.

interactions.label: Time (Seconds)
interactions.effect: Moves a vertical red timeline cursor across the spatio-temporal plots while simultaneously updating the animated positions of the pedestrians in the scene.
interactions.teaches: How real-time physical movement around the corner directly maps to a specific temporal slice of the angle-vs-time trajectory plot.

interactions.label: Number of People
interactions.effect: Toggles between a single walking person (matching panel c) and two crossing people (matching panel d).
interactions.teaches: How overlapping trajectories in the spatio-temporal plot correspond to multiple independent light sources crossing paths.

interactions.label: Signal Gain
interactions.effect: Amplifies the visual contrast of the penumbra on the ground tiles near the corner, transitioning from nearly invisible (raw) to highly enhanced.
interactions.teaches: Why computational processing is required: the raw optical signal is extremely faint and buried in ambient noise, but amplification reveals a structured angular shadow.

demo_steps.title: The Corner Camera Setup
demo_steps.narration: Look at the camera on the tripod in panel (a). It is pointing at the ground near the corner of a building, completely blocking its line of sight to the alley in panel (b). By focusing on the ground tiles, we can capture light reflecting from the hidden scene.
demo_steps.focus: The physical camera positioning in (a) relative to the hidden pedestrians in (b).

demo_steps.title: Revealing the Hidden Signal
demo_steps.narration: To the naked eye, the ground looks uniformly lit. Drag the Signal Gain slider up to enhance the contrast. Notice how a faint, moving shadow zone (penumbra) appears on the floor. The vertical edge of the wall acts as an aperture, meaning each point on the ground receives light from a restricted wedge of angles around the corner.
demo_steps.focus: The ground tiles near the base of the corner wall where the camera is aimed.

demo_steps.title: Tracking a Single Path
demo_steps.narration: Set the Time slider to scrub through the pedestrian's walk. Watch how their physical angular position in (b) maps to the dark sinusoidal wave in the spatio-temporal plot (c). When they walk closer to the corner, their angular range changes rapidly, creating a steep slope in the black trajectory line.
demo_steps.focus: The correspondence between the person's physical angle in (b) and the vertical axis (angle) of the plot in (c).

demo_steps.title: Resolving Multiple Subjects
demo_steps.narration: Now increase the number of people to 2. As they walk past each other, observe how their trajectories cross in panel (d). Even though the light signals blend together on the ground, the computational corner-camera can still reconstruct and track both distinct paths independently.
demo_steps.focus: The X-shaped intersection in the spatio-temporal plot (d) representing two crossing targets.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: The visualization should be divided into a top section (3D scene views) and a bottom section (spatio-temporal plots). The top-left view replicates panel (a) with a camera on a tripod pointed at a wall corner's ground plane. The top-right view replicates panel (b), showing a top-down or high-angle perspective of the hidden area where 1 or 2 colored circular markers (representing pedestrians) walk along sinusoidal paths. The bottom section displays the spatio-temporal plots matching (c) and (d), with the vertical axis labeled 'angle (theta)' and the horizontal axis labeled 'time'. These plots should feature a colorful, highly-textured/noisy background (red, green, blue noise) with distinct dark, thick bands tracing the sinusoidal trajectories of the moving markers, complete with a draggable vertical timeline cursor.
